headline: Iran says two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
summary: On Saturday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, each reportedly carrying around 2 million barrels of crude. There was no independent confirmation. The strait normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil, and attacks on ships there have kept oil above $100 a barrel. For India, which imports most of its oil, every new incident raises the risk of costlier fuel and freight.
concept_note: Each attack makes it harder to move oil, so less is supplied at every price: the supply curve shifts left, and the price rises even though demand hasn't changed.
source_name: AFP via Daily Tribune (also reported by Reuters)

headline: IMF members call the world economy resilient, but warn of wars, debt and AI risks
summary: At the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok on Saturday, the committee that steers the IMF said the global economy is showing "remarkable resilience" but that "there is no room for complacency". Its chair, Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, listed the risks: wars, threats to energy and food supplies, high public debt and fast-moving AI. Nearly half the delegates walked out during the Russian finance minister's speech.
concept_note: These are macro-environment forces (PESTLE): political (wars), economic (debt, energy prices) and technological (AI). No single company controls them, yet every company's plans depend on them.

headline: Jio Platforms' ₹30,213-crore IPO opens Wednesday; brokerages say subscribe
summary: Jio Platforms, Reliance's telecom and digital arm, will sell new shares worth about ₹30,213 crore at ₹1,065–1,119 each, from 21 to 23 October, with listing expected on 28 October. Most of the money, ₹27,500 crore, will repay Reliance Jio's borrowings. Brokerages including Emkay, GEPL and Ventura recommend subscribing, pointing to steady profit growth and falling capital spending: capex dropped from 48.8% of revenue in FY24 to 23.3% in FY26.
concept_note: Building towers and buying spectrum is capital expenditure: it creates assets that earn for years. As that spending falls as a share of revenue, more cash is left over, which is one reason analysts like the issue.

headline: Durga Puja's two economies: malls boom while small traders feel the pinch
summary: This Puja, the festival economy is growing, but unevenly. Kolkata mall operator Primarc Projects reported 17% more footfall in the 45 days before the festival, and big puja committees say advertising rates are up at least 20%. Meanwhile about 30% of outdoor ad slots at smaller pujas stayed empty, and hawkers in Burrabazar, Hatibagan and Shyambazar report shrinking margins. Traders' associations blame deep online discounts for pulling buyers away.
concept_note: Buyers no longer go straight from need to the nearest shop: they search online, compare prices and chase discounts first. When the decision process changes, where the money goes changes too.
teaser_title: This Puja, the malls are busier, while the hawkers of Hatibagan are squeezed.
teaser: Same festival, same crowds, two very different Pujas. Mall footfall jumped 17% before the festival, while hawkers in Hatibagan, Burrabazar and Shyambazar say their margins are shrinking. Here's where the Puja money is really going, and the one marketing idea that explains it.

headline: HDFC Bank's profit rises 4.7% as bad loans fall
summary: HDFC Bank, India's largest private bank and a major campus recruiter, reported a standalone net profit of ₹19,510 crore for July–September, up 4.7% from a year ago. Net interest income, what it earns on loans minus what it pays on deposits, rose 9.7% to ₹34,619 crore. Deposits grew 18.8% and loans 16.3%. Gross bad loans fell to 1.11% of loans, but profit growth was held back by a 67% drop in treasury trading gains, to ₹780 crore.
concept_note: Each figure has a home in the statements: net interest income and profit in the profit and loss statement; deposits (what the bank owes) and loans (what it is owed) in the balance sheet.
